content.title: CBT for Trauma Training
content.subtitle: Two-year course - training trauma therapists in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT)
content.summary: A two-year program in cognitive behavioral therapy for trauma: the first year on simple trauma, the second year on complex trauma.
content.description:
Participants will acquire the skills needed for assessment and treatment using cognitive behavioral therapy according to the three-phase model.

## First year - simple trauma

The course will focus on treating simple trauma - trauma caused by exposure to a single event in adulthood. During the first year, we teach trauma assessment tools, structuring treatment and case conceptualization according to CBT principles, and the three-phase model of trauma treatment, including emotion regulation, various exposure techniques and cognitive interventions.

## Second year - treating complex trauma

Complex post-traumatic stress disorder is caused by exposure to multiple or prolonged traumatic events, such as captivity, prolonged combat, domestic violence, abuse or neglect in childhood.

Therapists frequently encounter symptoms such as difficulty trusting, a tendency toward self-destructiveness, alexithymia (difficulty putting feelings into words), chronic depression, symptoms associated with borderline personality disorder, or dissociative symptoms. Many of these symptoms can be attributed to complex trauma, and they are often resistant to conventional treatment.

Pierre Janet developed the three-phase model for treating such disorders in the 19th century. His model has since been adapted and developed by modern clinicians (e.g., van der Hart). Many people coping with complex trauma suffer from a wide range of co-occurring disorders, such as substance abuse, poor social skills and anxiety disorders, which must be treated before the trauma itself can be addressed. This makes treating complex trauma longer and more complicated than usual. This training teaches methods for treating severe personality disorders.

During the second year, we focus on complex trauma, which in many cases is accompanied by anxiety disorders, depression, complex personality disorders such as borderline personality disorder, dissociative disorders, difficulties with impulse control, and difficulty functioning independently. The second year provides a theoretical framework for understanding these disorders in the context of trauma and in other contexts, along with practical training in therapeutic tools such as mindfulness, DBT, schema therapy and ACT.

## Program details

Our training course combines methods from classic cognitive behavioral therapy (exposure methods, e.g., Foa and others; cognitive therapy, e.g., Clark, Ehlers and others), integrating them into the three-phase model of trauma treatment (Janet, van der Hart). This model sequences the interventions so that the client is not flooded by painful memories before learning to regulate their level of arousal. Our training emphasizes mind-body approaches and includes third-wave CBT models such as mindfulness, DBT and acceptance and commitment therapy.

Teaching methods include lectures, reading and discussing academic papers, live demonstrations and films, practicing the techniques taught, and clinical supervision on cases. The treatment methods taught are used in treating trauma as well as anxiety disorders, dissociative disorders, depression and other disorders.

items: Phenomenology of trauma
Cognitive effects of trauma

Acute stress disorder (ASD)

Models of cognitive behavioral therapy

Phenomenology: characteristics and assessment of complex trauma disorders
Complex trauma and depression: assessing and treating depression and traumatic grief

Trauma and destructiveness: treating impulse-control problems and impulsivity, treating addiction
Trauma and difficulties in building the therapeutic relationship: cognitive behavioral strategies for building trust, cooperation and commitment to treatment goals

Trauma and the body: body image, health concerns, eating disorders, and the effect of trauma on sexuality
Trauma and dissociation: phenomenology, assessment and treatment based on the structural dissociation model (Prof. van der Hart)
Trauma, psychiatric crises and psychosis
Methods taught in the course include mindfulness according to Segal and Kabat-Zinn, ACT according to Hayes, and schema therapy according to Young

content.title: The Roadmap for Trauma Therapy
content.subtitle: Practical tools for trauma therapy - a course for therapists, in person and on Zoom
content.summary: A four-session course on trauma processes, therapeutic compasses and the components of trauma therapy work. Held in in-person and Zoom cohorts.
content.description:
At Metiv, the center for the treatment of psychological trauma, we have been treating, researching and teaching trauma therapy for 30 years. Over these years, the understanding of psychological trauma and its treatment has changed, and recent years in Israel have challenged these approaches even further as we encounter many manifestations of trauma's effects. There are many protocols for treating trauma, but the expected magic often does not happen in the clinic.

In our work with trauma survivors, we see that a deep and broad understanding of trauma's effects on the brain and body is needed, along with its thoughtful and flexible application. Trauma therapy often creates helplessness and situations of being stuck, and the tools we are used to are not enough to bring about change.

The Roadmap for Trauma Therapy course:

- Was built from our long and varied experience, and lays out guidelines, compasses and a toolbox that together help therapists find their way through the tangle of trauma and make decisions that move treatment forward - what is right to do and when - and also addresses the therapist's own therapeutic stance at every stage of treatment.
- Lays a stable, deep foundation that gives an understanding of direction and path, of the phases, and of working with different trauma presentations.
- Includes theoretical knowledge and extensive clinical experience, as well as exercises that ground the understanding in practice.

The course is practical, not only theoretical, and allows therapists to understand in depth, acquire skills, grow more confident in their work, and develop the ability to work in varied ways within the complex field of trauma.

After the course, you can join a 5-session supervision group in which participants can bring cases from their practice for consultation and work planning, and learn from other participants' cases. Additional fee; subject to the number of participants.

rows.title: The Foundations of Treating Complex Trauma

content.title: The Foundations of Treating Complex Trauma
content.subtitle: When trauma is embedded in the body and in relationships, a different therapeutic roadmap is needed. An advanced course for therapists.
content.summary: An advanced 6-session course for therapists who work with survivors of complex trauma, following on from The Roadmap course or equivalent courses.
content.description:
Complex trauma is a phenomenon familiar both from the clinic and from the professional literature. It usually results from prolonged or repeated exposure to traumatic events in childhood - often within significant relationships. Unlike single-incident trauma, it becomes intertwined with central developmental processes and affects the formation of identity, self-image, relationships with others and the experience of the world as a whole.

In these situations we see deep disruption of regulation systems, disconnection between the body and awareness, complex dissociative phenomena, somatization, harm to sexual self-image and functioning, and sometimes also an absence of narrative memory of the trauma - all of which make the processing harder and also shake the therapeutic relationship.

In this course we will offer a clinical and therapeutic roadmap for meeting this challenge. Drawing on extensive experience working with clients who suffer from complex trauma, we have developed an integrated treatment model that uses tools from the psychodynamic approach, from third-wave CBT, and from body and movement work. This combination makes it possible to address emotional and bodily regulation systems, strengthen the capacity for containment, improve relationships and broaden the inner interpretation of stimuli - on the way to a life with a sense of coherence and meaning.

units.title: Dissociation and Trauma

lecturers.name: Danny Brom
lecturers.role: Founder of the trauma center, an international expert in trauma therapy

units.description:
Dissociation is a special mechanism, inherent to trauma, that helps a person in survival mode avoid encountering unbearable horror. Sometimes the situation becomes more complicated and over time creates splits of various kinds, which disrupt and damage everyday life.

Danny Brom will talk about how to identify and how to work with dissociative states.

units.title: Meeting at the Heart of the Rupture - Treating Traumatic Grief
units.tagline: The loss of someone close is a tear in the personal fabric of our lives.

lecturers.name: Nili Lavie
lecturers.role: Expert clinical psychologist

units.description:
When a loss occurs in sudden, violent or traumatic circumstances, it is an experience that shakes the psyche and a person's connection with themselves and with others, an experience that creates particular complexity and difficulties in the grieving process.

Led by Nili Lavie, we will spend the day delving into the experience of traumatic grief and its treatment, with the aim of deepening professional understanding and the courage to come into contact with one of the most painful experiences we encounter as therapists and as human beings, and perhaps also to offer an opening for connection and meaning.

units.title: A Workshop on Using Art for Therapists Who Are Not Art Therapists
units.tagline: "Where there are no words, there is material, color, blot and line"

lecturers.name: Tamara Weiner
lecturers.role: Art therapist and Focusing-oriented psychotherapist, Focusing teacher, therapist and supervisor at the trauma center

units.description:
Survival mode disconnects us from the parts of the brain responsible for language, so we often meet trauma survivors who find it hard to talk and express themselves in words. Art materials offer a rich, grounded language for expressing the traumatic experience and foster processes of regulation, processing and integration in trauma therapy.

Tamara Weiner will present ways of addressing trauma through art, even when your specialty is not art therapy.

units.title: ACT for Trauma Therapy
units.tagline: How can acceptance and commitment be integrated into therapy with people who have experienced trauma?

lecturers.name: Dalia Zivan
lecturers.role: Trauma therapist, lecturer and supervisor. Clinical director of the MDMA/SEA-IT study at Metiv

units.description:
In this course we will learn the basic principles of the ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) approach and explore ways of integrating them into work with people who have experienced trauma. The course is an introduction offering a first exposure to the approach, focusing on trauma-related avoidance patterns, working with painful emotions, and using values as a central tool for promoting change.

The course is suitable for therapists who want to get to know the ACT approach and expand their tools for working with trauma.

units.title: "Not by Talk Alone"
units.tagline: An experiential workshop in which we will learn how to integrate the different modes of experience into trauma therapy
units.description:
In extreme situations we see how the components of experience become disconnected from one another, for example emotion disconnecting from functioning, and sometimes components become over-coupled, such as an image or situation that is always accompanied by intense fear.

This process requires trauma therapy to address each component of experience separately and to allow appropriate connections between them, in order to restore the integrative capacity damaged by the trauma and to distinguish what belongs to the present and what to past events.

In the workshop we will learn tools and techniques for integrating this work with the various modes of experience - senses, images, movements and more - in therapy with trauma survivors.

units.title: Treating Sexual Trauma

lecturers.name: Michal Zmora
lecturers.role: Head of the courses unit, trauma therapist, lecturer and supervisor

units.description:
Sexual trauma is a particularly sensitive and complex subject. Beyond the threat to life it sometimes involves, it also involves a violation of basic trust in other people, and it is usually accompanied by guilt and shame.

Michal Zmora will talk about this complex condition and its treatment.

units.title: Childbirth - "Birth Stories"
units.description:
Childbirth and "birth stories" usually get the public image of an uplifting, mainly joyful event. Yet despite this, and sometimes precisely because of it, about a third of women who give birth will experience the birth as traumatic.

Together we will learn about treating women after childbirth, and about guiding directions for processing and working with births of all kinds (including working with pregnancy loss and stillbirth). We will look in depth at the different experiences, the meaning of the high numbers, and the various causes and consequences.

units.title: Narrative Work with Post-Traumatic Stress
units.tagline: Narrative work as part of trauma therapy

lecturers.name: Dr. Michal Simchon
lecturers.role: PhD in bibliotherapy, former head of the bibliotherapy department at David Yellin College, longtime therapist at Metiv

units.description:
Narrative therapy is about expanding the confining stories a person sometimes tells about themselves and about the world.

In cases of trauma and loss, beyond the pain, the suffering and the torment, the sense of identity is also harmed. The person feels weak, helpless, hopeless and sometimes guilty as well. In addition, the traumatic event remains in body and mind as if in tatters, and the memories spread and remain without narrative continuity.

In the course we will learn the principles of narrative therapy and get to know various narrative means through which a person's dignity, identity and story can be restored to them. The course will combine theoretical study, clinical examples and personal experiential exercises. Michal Simchon will present tools for stitching together and expanding the post-traumatic narrative, and for working with the narrative when it is stuck and harmful.

units.title: Compassion Fatigue: Its Impact on the Therapist and the Therapist's Role

Trauma therapy requires the therapist to have a variety of skills and the ability to apply them flexibly with the particular client in the clinic and their unique situation. To support therapists' skills and the tailored use of the tools taught in our course, we are opening a day devoted entirely to practicing the skills acquired in the course - psychoeducation, grounding, attention and regulation skills, and integrative connection of the components of experience, including the bodily component.

content.title: Metiv's Annual Course Program
content.subtitle: Metiv's courses unit presents the 2025 curriculum
content.summary: An overview of the courses, learning units, supervision and learning community that Metiv published for 2025, with general information on joining.
content.description:
You are invited to join us in person and remotely for courses on trauma. The program includes courses for thorough, comprehensive learning, advanced courses in trauma therapy, supervision options, and joining Metiv's learning community.

Metiv has been operating as a training center for more than 20 years, training therapists, organizations and professionals from a range of fields. The programs are based on broad clinical knowledge and experience, combined with treatment methods from Israel and around the world. To date, more than 2,000 therapists have been trained. The trainings are also offered online.

## What the 2025 program includes

- **Advanced courses, in-depth study and learning units** - Kaleidoscope units: Narrative Work with Post-Traumatic Stress, "Not by Talk Alone", ACT for Trauma Therapy. Coming soon: Trauma on the Continuum, Moral Injury, Psychedelics and Trauma Therapy, Compassion Fatigue: Its Impact on the Therapist and the Therapist's Role.
- **Short, focused, practical courses** - The Roadmap (June), The Roadmap for public bodies and nonprofits (contact shir@metiv.org), a one-day course: Building a Trauma-Informed Organization.
- **Learning community** - Journal Club: a learning community on trauma research and treatment, free of charge. Individual supervision (NIS 450) and a supervision group.

content.title: International Summer Course
content.subtitle: Trauma and Resilience from the Israeli Perspective - Theory and Practice
content.summary: A summer course in English, in partnership with the Hebrew University, on trauma and resilience in the Israeli context, with an optional third week of clinical training for therapists.
content.description:
The summer program, which lasts two to three weeks, is run in partnership with the Hebrew University and gives participants a comprehensive picture of the latest developments in the field of trauma in general, and in the Israeli context in particular. The course includes theoretical lectures, experiential learning and educational field trips.

Students learn about risk factors for developing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), symptoms of associated distress, and potential protective factors. The course presents theories and research on the effects of trauma, healthy coping processes and possible pathological consequences. Guiding principles for treating post-traumatic disorders are also discussed.

The field trips and lectures include meetings with researchers and professionals in the field of trauma.

## Optional follow-up week: clinical training in cognitive behavioral therapy for post-traumatic disorders

In addition to the course, an optional third week of clinical training is offered for therapists who want to specialize in trauma therapy (40 academic hours, 2 credits). This training is based on the three-phase model of trauma treatment. The first phase, stabilization, focuses on self-regulation techniques. The second phase, trauma processing, includes exposure techniques and building a narrative. The third phase, integration, calls for cognitive techniques. During the training week, students will review the literature in the field, discuss the treatment model, watch demonstrations of the techniques and practice them with one another by working with their own personal experiences.

**Please note: the course is taught in English. The third week is for therapists only.**

At the same time, we will learn treatment approaches based on combining different methods - TF-CBT, CPP, SE - and on combining these therapeutic approaches with play.

The course will be taught by Sarit Schramm-Yavin, an expert educational psychologist and director of Metiv Children.

content.title: Training for Therapists: PANDA for Elementary School Children
content.subtitle: A training track for PANDA group facilitators, for ages 7-12
content.summary: Training in facilitating emotion regulation groups using the PANDA model for elementary school-age children.
content.description:
The course is for therapists who want to specialize in leading emotion regulation groups using the PANDA group model (PANDA, a Hebrew acronym for "Here We Learn Ways of Coping"). The course will combine theoretical learning with hands-on experience of exercises from the program, so that by the end of the course participants will be able to facilitate PANDA groups in a variety of settings for elementary school-age children.

## Background on the PANDA program

The PANDA program - "Here We Learn Ways of Coping" - helps children and parents develop their emotion regulation abilities and ways of coping. The program is run in a group, is designed for children aged 7-12, and includes 8 sessions for children and 3 sessions for parents. The program combines mindfulness techniques, cognitive-behavioral techniques and narrative interventions, all woven into the program in a creative and enjoyable way.

What sets PANDA apart from similar programs is that it is designed for every child, not only for children who show worrying behaviors or are experiencing significant difficulty. The program's basic premise is that everyone can benefit from emotion regulation tools, and that these tools will stay with them throughout their lives.

The PANDA program was developed by Prof. Ruth Pat-Horenczyk and Sarit Schramm-Yavin at "Metiv - The Israel Psychotrauma Center".

content.title: PANDA for Parents - A Training Track for Therapists
content.summary: A 12-academic-hour course for therapists who work with parents, on facilitating PANDA for Parents groups.
content.description:
The course is for mental health therapists who work with parents and parenting and want to expand their professional toolbox and run PANDA for Parents groups.

The course includes three sessions of four academic hours each, for a total of 12 academic hours. The curriculum covers content on trauma, emotion regulation and parenting, an introduction to DBT skills, and practice of mindfulness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance and interpersonal skills. The course will also discuss the process of building a group, recruiting participants and evaluating the program.

## Background on the PANDA for Parents program

PANDA for Parents groups were developed by Sarit Schramm-Yavin and Tzipora Hayat as a follow-on to the PANDA program ("Here We Learn Ways of Coping") for ages 7-12, out of the understanding that parenting can challenge our ability to cope with stress and can intensify mood swings. By its very nature, parenting confronts parents with frustration, uncertainty, helplessness and even despair. The program aims to teach practical emotion regulation tools that can help in coping with challenging parenting situations. The program is based on the dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) approach, which includes practical tools for regulating emotions, coping with stressful situations and managing relationships with others, and includes exercises from the PANDA for Children program.

rows.title: PANDA for Two - A Training Track for Parent-Child Group Facilitators

content.title: PANDA for Two - A Training Track for Parent-Child Group Facilitators
content.summary: Training for early childhood therapists in facilitating dyadic groups for parents and toddlers, in a reworked version of the NAMAL program.
content.description:
The course is for early childhood therapists who want to specialize in leading PANDA for Two groups (formerly NAMAL - "Let's Make Room for Play"). The course will combine theoretical learning with hands-on experience of exercises from the program, so that by the end of the course participants will be able to facilitate PANDA groups in a variety of settings.

## Training stages

- Part A: PANDA for Two course, 24 academic hours.
- Part B: Implementing the PANDA for Two model with supervision from Metiv Children, 6 group supervision sessions.

## Background on the PANDA for Two program

The PANDA for Two program is a reworking of the "Let's Make Room for Play" (NAMAL) program, developed by Prof. Esther Cohen and Prof. Ruth Pat-Horenczyk for Metiv. It is a model of play-focused group work for pairs of parents and young children, aimed at developing parents' playfulness and capacity for abstraction so that they can promote and support the development of regulation abilities in their children.

The program is designed for parent-toddler pairs aged 2-3 who are dealing with difficulties typical of this age and/or are exposed to stress, crisis or trauma. The program includes 6 parent-and-child sessions for about 8 dyads. Each session has a psychoeducational message aimed at parents and expressed in a short, catchy saying. The messages are conveyed through shared play, music, drama and movement activities suited to ages 2-3.

## The program's key messages

- **The parent-child bond** as a protective, secure base
- **Encouraging independence and self-confidence**
- **Playfulness**, humor and creativity
- **Reflecting** actions and intentions
- **Expressing and reflecting emotions**

content.title: Building a Trauma-Informed Organization
content.subtitle: A one-day course for HR managers and organizational consultants
content.summary: A one-day course as part of "Metiv Space" on the effects of trauma on employees, clients and organizations, and on adapting procedures and processes.
content.description:
The October 7 disaster, the Iron Swords war and the turbulent reality we have been living through since then affect us as individuals and as a society. This impact is also felt in the workplace.

Are you also encountering the impact of trauma in your organization?

- Difficulty returning to routine among employees back from reserve duty
- Heightened anxiety and difficulty functioning among employees and clients
- Extreme reactions by clients to trauma-triggering situations, such as how service providers treat them
- Impatience, anger and disproportionate reactions to frustrating situations among employees and clients

Metiv, the Israel Psychotrauma Center, invites you to an intensive one-day course: "Metiv Space" - developing a trauma-informed organization. In the course you will broaden your understanding of trauma and its effects on employees and clients, and receive tools for leading your organization as a trauma-informed one.

Light refreshments will be served during the day. Dates for upcoming courses will be announced.
content.location: 8 Eliezer Kaplan St., Fiverr offices (a 15-minute walk from Tel Aviv HaShalom train station). No parking on site.
